evidence.summary: pay() calls gateway.charge(order['amount'], key or str(id(order))) and stores the returned charge id on the order
pay() sets order['paid'] = True only after charge() returns; nothing catches a gateway error, and there is no check that the order is already paid
on_webhook() sets order['paid'] = True on every delivery; it reads no event field (no id, no type) and its own comment says every delivery applies again
The user describes Billfold as charging cards through a payment gateway and receiving its webhooks

features.name: Charge an order through the payment gateway
features.description: Charges the order's amount through the gateway with an idempotency key and records the charge id
features.observed_behaviour: pay(gateway, order, key) calls gateway.charge(amount, key or str(id(order))), stores charge_id, then sets paid = True
features.business_logic: Idempotency key is the caller's key, else str(id(order)) (a process memory address, not stable across retries or processes). No already-paid check, so a second pay with a different key charges again. A gateway exception propagates and leaves paid unset even if the charge went through.
features.integration: payment gateway adapter (charge with idempotency key)

features.name: Receive payment gateway webhooks
features.description: Marks an order paid when the gateway sends a webhook
features.observed_behaviour: on_webhook(order, event) sets paid = True; the event is not inspected
features.business_logic: No deduplication by event id: every delivery (including retries) applies again. Event type is ignored, so a refund event would also mark the order paid.

entities.name: Order
entities.description: A payable order as Billfold sees it: an amount, a charge id and a paid flag (an in-memory dict)

fields.name: amount
fields.description: amount passed to gateway.charge; unit not stated in the code

fields.name: paid
fields.description: true once charged or once any webhook arrives

integrations.name: payment gateway
integrations.provider: unknown (passed in as an object with charge(amount, key))
integrations.idempotency: charges: caller key or str(id(order)); webhooks: none

error_handling.case: gateway raises (for example a timeout after the charge went through)
error_handling.behaviour: exception propagates; order keeps no charge id and paid stays unset although the gateway may have charged

architecture.backend: two module-level functions operating on a dict

unknowns: Unit and currency of order['amount']: the code passes it straight to the gateway; the mock gateway names it amount_cents (from gateway.py, not from Billfold)
How webhooks reach on_webhook (no HTTP endpoint or signature check in the code) and the event format (the code reads no field)
Persistence: no store in the code; how Billfold saves orders is not shown
Refunds: Billfold has no refund code
Rights: task.md states no rights and there is no licence file, so code_reuse is unknown and nothing is copied
